source.title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Akarsh Kumar; Jeff Clune; Joel Lehman; Kenneth O. Stanley

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses representational optimism and presents experiments on fractured versus unified representations, but does not measure convergence or similarity between models, or test how such alignment changes with scale, capability, or similarity settings.
record.gate_note: The paper's CPPN experiments compare internal organization and weight-perturbation behavior for evolved networks and SGD-trained networks that produce the same images. These bear on representation generally, but do not measure the inter-model alignment named by the claim versions. The GPT and image-generation examples are behavioral illustrations of FER, not measures of representational convergence; results cited from other work are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: A position paper on the fractured entangled representation (FER) hypothesis. Its own experiments compare one human-guided evolved CPPN with one SGD-trained CPPN of the same layerized architecture, both producing the same image. It does so qualitatively, through neuron activation visualizations and weight sweeps. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as an example of representational optimism, but it uses no inter-model similarity metric, no scale or capability sweep, no seed comparison, no mapping or stitching test and no cross-model feature-recurrence test. Its finding that functionally identical networks differ sharply inside concerns representation quality (unified vs fractured), not measured convergence, so it bears on no version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that identical output performance can hide very different internal representations, and that conventional SGD produces FER in their single-image CPPN experiments while open-ended evolution approaches UFR. They suggest FER may persist in large models and say the hope that it vanishes with scale merits scrutiny and further research. As a position paper, they state they propose no solution.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not apply a method for measuring inter-model representational convergence. Its experiments visualize CPPN activations and perturb weights to compare evolved and SGD-trained representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that PCA modestly changes the visual appearance of the SGD representation, but reports that it remains unlike the Picbreeder representation. Weight-sweep outcomes are also illustrated with selected weights; the authors point to the full sweep database.

fits_no_version.finding: Evolved (Picbreeder) and SGD-trained CPPNs give practically identical outputs for skull, butterfly and apple, but their internal organization and weight-perturbation behaviour differ radically. The SGD networks look fractured and entangled even with ReLU-only networks (Appendix E), after a PCA change of basis, and under random-direction weight sweeps (Appendix F).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks with identical input–output behaviour, reached by different training processes, can have qualitatively very different internal representations; functional equivalence does not imply representational similarity or equal adaptability.

record.problems: The central experiments use toy CPPNs for single-image targets and provide qualitative visualizations rather than a quantitative representation-alignment metric. The paper does not test scaling. Selected weight sweeps are illustrative, and the broader examples involving large models are not direct measurements of their internal representations.
record.rows_left_out: Behavioral anecdotes about counting, sequence substitution, and image generation were not extracted as rows because they are not measurements of inter-model representational convergence. Results from other cited studies were also excluded.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no alignment measured between independently trained models.
No vision–language or paired image–caption alignment.

No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different seeds for shared features or subspaces. The SGD networks are single runs per target (Figure 12's three seeds are on the raw architecture and fail to train).
No linear map, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired translation between the evolved and SGD networks.
No test of whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across models; feature organization is described separately for each network.
No comparison of similarity metrics, their settings or input distributions. The PCA basis change in Appendix F concerns how organization is visualized, not convergence measurement.
No measure of the degree of alignment, any plateau, or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and state cannot_determine. Their evidence is qualitative visualization of single networks, not cross-model similarity. The ReLU (Appendix E) and PCA/random-direction sweep (Appendix F) robustness checks are not rowed; they would also bear on no version. Researchers might read the paper as loosely relevant to the 'representational optimism' framing of V1, since it cites Huh et al. 2024. However, it measures representation quality, not convergence, and the comparison is one evolved network versus one SGD-trained network per target.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no measurement of representational alignment between independently trained models.
No paired image-caption representations or cross-modal alignment measurement.
No same-architecture training-seed comparison or shared-feature/subspace measurement.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No cross-model recurrence test for interpretable features or circuits.
No comparison of convergence metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No measurement of inter-model alignment, its plateau, or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the skull target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes symmetry emerging early and key features represented once.
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD CPPN trained to reproduce the same skull
rows.value: Organized, symmetric intermediate representations; 24 novel representations in the layerized version.
rows.note: This measures internal organization, not similarity or distance between independently trained models.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the skull target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes a disorganized patchwork, with symmetry appearing only at the output layer across 12 underlying layers.
rows.baseline: Picbreeder CPPN producing the same skull
rows.value: Disorganized intermediate patterns; symmetry is not represented until the output layer, as described in the text.
rows.note: The output image is described as effectively identical to the Picbreeder CPPN's; internal organization is assessed qualitatively.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weights and observed the resulting skull images.

conditions.value: selected individual weights swept from -1 through 0 to +1

rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; selected sweeps show meaningful semantic changes, usually preserving overall symmetry.
rows.baseline: Original skull output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Selected weights control interpretable changes including mouth opening, eye winking, eye width, and jaw width.
rows.note: The authors say the displayed sweeps were selected to show both methods in their best light and were broadly representative; the full sweep database is linked.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual weights and observed the resulting skull images.

conditions.value: selected individual weights swept from -1 through 0 to +1

rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; the text describes incoherent distortions and symmetry breaking.
rows.baseline: Original skull output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Selected sweeps produce meaningless distortions; the text says all weights lead to similarly meaningless perturbations.
rows.note: The paper treats these effects as evidence of FER, not as a measure of representational alignment.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the butterfly target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes early y-axis symmetry and each output aspect specified once.
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD CPPN trained to reproduce the same butterfly
rows.value: Organized representation with early symmetry, described as a UFR.
rows.note: No quantitative cross-model similarity measure is reported.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the butterfly target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes separately encoded wings and arbitrarily stitched high-frequency patterns.
rows.baseline: Picbreeder CPPN producing the same butterfly
rows.value: Disorganized representation lacking the butterfly's symmetry, described as FER.
rows.note: The output behavior is described as perfectly reconstructed despite the different internal organization.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weights and observed the resulting butterfly images.
rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; the text describes meaningful changes that preserve symmetry.
rows.baseline: Original butterfly output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Selected sweeps produce recognizable changes, including wing-area and color changes, while respecting symmetry.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weights and observed the resulting butterfly images.
rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; the text describes deleterious changes that often break symmetry.
rows.baseline: Original butterfly output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Sweeps yield deleterious changes and often break symmetry.
rows.note: This is a qualitative FER result, not a convergence measurement.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the apple target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes the stem and body encoded separately and later combined.
rows.baseline: Conventional SGD CPPN trained to reproduce the same apple
rows.value: A modular representation with separate stem, body, and background factors is described as a UFR.
rows.note: No quantitative cross-model similarity measure is reported.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activations across inputs for the apple target.
rows.measure: Qualitative organization of intermediate activations; the text describes intertwined processing without clear separation of apple, stem, and background.
rows.baseline: Picbreeder CPPN producing the same apple
rows.value: A fragmented, highly entangled representation is described as FER.
rows.note: The authors describe the SGD network as trained to reproduce the same apple output.

rows.subject: Picbreeder CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weights and observed the resulting apple images.
rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; the text describes weights that control components independently.
rows.baseline: Original apple output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Selected sweeps control stem angle, apple size, background, and stem removal; some changes are described as independent.
rows.note: Selected examples are qualitative; the text says the full set of sweeps is available at the code link.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept selected individual weights and observed the resulting apple images.
rows.measure: Qualitative changes in output under weight sweeps; the text describes entangled changes to multiple apple components.
rows.baseline: Original apple output at the unperturbed weight setting
rows.value: Sweeps often change several concepts together, such as apple size with stem changes or background color with stem color.
rows.note: This is a qualitative finding about entanglement, not cross-model alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
